one_liner: Small OpenMP-parallel C PNG encoder with stored, Huffman-only and RLE deflate paths; about 11x faster than libpng single-threaded in those modes.
what_it_does: Encodes 8- or 16-bit gray, gray+alpha, RGB or RGBA rasters (with row stride) to PNG. The API is pngenc_write_file(desc, filename), or pngenc_create_encoder(threads, chunk_size) plus pngenc_encode(encoder, desc, callback, user_data), which streams IDAT chunks to a write callback. It is not libpng-API compatible: it only encodes, writes only IHDR/IDAT/IEND (no palette, interlace, sub-8-bit depths or gAMA/iCCP/sRGB/tEXt chunks), and offers four strategies: no compression, Huffman-only, RLE, and AUTO (Huffman-only, switching to RLE when a chunk is mostly zero bytes).
how_it_is_fast: It skips LZ77 match search entirely: every row gets the fixed Sub filter (no per-row filter heuristic), then either literal-only Huffman coding (like zlib Z_HUFFMAN_ONLY) or distance-1 run-length matches (like Z_RLE), with length-limited canonical codes built from a 4-way 16-bit-counter histogram and an encoder that packs three codes per 64-bit window with unaligned stores. The image is cut into row chunks (default 512 KiB of filtered data); OpenMP threads encode the chunks in parallel as independent byte-aligned deflate blocks (each ended with an empty stored block, as a zlib sync flush does), emit them in order as separate IDAT chunks, and merge per-chunk checksums with adler32_combine. Checksums use AVX2 Adler-32 (adapted from a fork of fpng) and PCLMULQDQ CRC-32 folding (Intel white-paper method).
when_to_use: Dumping screenshots, frame captures, render or debug outputs to valid 8-bit PNG where latency matters more than file size.
Multi-core x86-64 machines that can put all cores on one image: the README reports 1.2 ms for a Huffman-only 1080p RGB frame with OpenMP vs 82 ms for libpng.
Streaming output: the callback API hands out each IDAT chunk as soon as its turn comes, so no full compressed buffer is needed.
Vendoring a zlib-licensed C encoder (about ten source files) that does not depend on zlib or libpng.
when_not_to_use: Size-competitive PNGs: there is no LZ77 mode, the README's Full LZ77 row has no pngenc number, and the 'same compression rates as libpng/zlib' claim comes with no file sizes.

16-bit images in Huffman-only, RLE or AUTO mode: a byte-swap bug makes them decode to wrong pixel values (see gotchas). In the uncompressed mode 16-bit samples are copied in host order with no big-endian swap.
Small or highly compressible images: a compressed chunk of roughly 64 to 103 bytes can get a wrong IDAT CRC (see gotchas), which strict decoders such as libpng reject.
Portable binaries or big-endian targets: x86 builds use -march=native or /arch:AVX2, and the chunk and stored-block headers are written by copying little-endian structs.
Projects that need maintenance: it is a self-described hobby project with 3 stars and its last commit was on 2024-08-10.

integration.form: shared lib (CMake add_library SHARED) or source-drop of the source/pngenc/*.c files
integration.dependencies: libc and OpenMP (libgomp, libomp or MSVC /openmp)
integration.min_toolchain: C99 (-std=gnu99), CMake 3.0; README says tested with GCC/MinGW, Clang and MSVC
integration.platforms: little-endian x86-64 (AVX2 Adler-32 and PCLMUL CRC-32 chosen at run time, but the intrinsics are compiled in unconditionally, so a GCC/Clang build needs an AVX2/PCLMUL build host for -march=native to accept them); ARM via scalar paths plus -mfpu=neon on armv7l (commit 'Fix non-x86 builds', 2022-12-07)
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. An encoder owns per-thread scratch buffers, so share one encoder only serially. Each encode is internally parallel and calls omp_set_num_threads, which changes the calling thread's OpenMP setting.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — different API (descriptor plus callback) and encoder only; it matches libpng only when libpng is run with the Z_HUFFMAN_ONLY or Z_RLE strategies or at level 0

gotchas: 16-bit correctness bug (splitter.c, prepare_data_filtered): after the Sub filter, the byte-swap loop stores dst[i+1] = src[i] (the raw low byte) instead of the filtered byte, so for every pixel after the first in a row, low bytes accumulate on decode (reproduced with a Python re-implementation of the loop: 0x1234 0x5678 0x9ABC decodes as 0x1268 0x56f0 0x9a78 in the second pixel). The 16-bit integration test only checks the return code and uses byte-symmetric values (0x0000, 0x8888, 0xFFFF), so it cannot catch this.

CRC bug (crc32.c, crc32_hw): when len >= 64 but fewer than 64 bytes remain after aligning to 64 bytes, crc32_pclmul still folds a full 64-byte block (aligned_len = 0 is not checked), so those bytes are counted twice and the IDAT CRC is wrong. Chunk data starts 8 bytes into a 16-byte-aligned buffer, so short compressed chunks (about 64 to 103 bytes with glibc's mmap alignment) are affected. Large 1080p chunks are not, so the README numbers stand.

MSVC x64 only: the SSE2 Sub-filter loop tests i < bytes_per_row - 32 in uint64_t, which wraps around for rows narrower than 32 bytes and reads and writes out of bounds; rows of exactly 32 bytes read src[-c].
pngenc_create_encoder does not check its malloc results, pngenc_write_file leaks the encoder when encoding fails, and every encoder creation rewrites a global CRC table and CPU-feature flags.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: fpnge and fpng are faster per core and compress better (in the QOIR benchmark fpnge encodes about 57x faster than libpng with files about 15% larger), and mtpng parallelizes full deflate; pick pngenc only if you specifically want OpenMP-parallel Huffman-only or RLE encoding of 8-bit images from a tiny zlib-licensed C codebase and can accept those file sizes.
verified_claims_summary: The author's README table (one unpublished 1920x1080 8-bit RGB image, Ryzen 7 3700X) gives Huffman-only 7.3 ms single-threaded vs 82 ms for libpng 1.6 (about 11x), RLE 30 vs 84 ms (2.8x) and uncompressed 0.8 vs 9 ms, and 1.2, 4 and 0.2 ms multi-threaded (ratios derived from page data). No compiler, flags, libpng filter or zlib settings, or libpng harness are published, and the repo's perf_mt.c only times pngenc 20 times into a null callback on a data.bin that is not in the repo. The bugs found affect 16-bit images and short chunks, not the 8-bit 1080p numbers.
status_note: Stale (last commit 2024-08-10, which added PNGENC_AUTO; 3 stars; one issue, a closed 2022 ASan odr-violation report) but zlib-licensed and small enough to vendor, provided you fix the 16-bit swap and the short-buffer CRC path, or keep to 8-bit images.
